why:
The criterion holds. I checked every command in both briefs against the tracked files and the scripts in package.json.
- `npm test` maps to `node --test`, which finds test/greet.test.js.
- bin/greet.js exists, so `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada`, `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`, `node bin/greet.js Ada`/`Grace` and the no-argument run are all valid.
- `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` is valid: `--` stops grep reading the pattern as an option, and the file exists.
- `gh run list --workflow pages.yml` names a workflow file that exists.
- `curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/` is valid syntax.
- `gh pr view <number> --json state,mergedAt` is marked "e.g.", and `<number>` is a stand-in for the PR number the verifier will have. Typed literally, the shell would read `<number>` as a redirect, but the flags and fields themselves are valid.
- The worktree step gives no command, so there is nothing to break.
- `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` in builder step 4 is text for the docs page, not a command to run.

No command names a missing file or has bad syntax.
